editorial:
Imagine a man who dreamed of the moon but helped start a war. You get to follow the life of Dr. Werner von Braun, a genius who loved rockets more than almost anything else. The movie feels like a classic old-school drama, taking you from his early days of experimenting with explosions to his time working for the Nazis during World War II. It is a wild ride because you see him as both a visionary and a man making some very scary choices just to see his rockets fly. The vibe is tense but fascinating, as you watch him balance his personal goals with the chaos of global war.

You will really appreciate the acting here, as the lead manages to make a complicated man feel human. The pacing is steady, though some of the middle parts might feel a bit slow if you are used to modern action movies. It is a great pick if you love history or science. If you want the best experience, try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection to see those old rocket launches in the best quality possible. It is a solid look at how one man's brain changed the world.
endingExplained: The story wraps up by showing von Braun moving to America after the war. You see him transition from a weapon maker for Germany to a hero for the US space program. The movie ends with him looking toward the stars, showing that his dream of space travel finally won out over the darkness of the war. He finds peace by helping humans reach the moon, leaving his controversial past behind him.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves history and the early days of space travel
